result.topic_en: Euler finds the four roots of the characteristic equation λ^4 = 1/f^4, writes the general solution of the fourth-order equation for the vibrating rod as exponentials plus sine and cosine of s/f, and multiplies it by a time-periodic factor to obtain a separated solution showing that the motion is like that of a simple pendulum.
result.transcription:
$\lambda^4 = \frac{1}{f^4}$, vnde ſequentes quatuor valores pro litera $\lambda$ eliciuntur, ſcilicet:
$1^\circ.\ \lambda = \frac{1}{f}$; $2^\circ.\ \lambda = -\frac{1}{f}$; $3^\circ.\ \lambda = \frac{\sqrt{-1}}{f}$; $4^\circ.\ \lambda = -\frac{\sqrt{-1}}{f}$,
quibus valoribus inuentis conſtat, eos etiam vtcunque combinatos ſatisfacere, ita vt ſtatuere queamus
$$y = \alpha e^{\frac{s}{f}} + \beta e^{\frac{-s}{f}} + \gamma e^{\frac{s\sqrt{-1}}{f}} + \delta e^{-\frac{s\sqrt{-1}}{f}},$$
quae forma, cum quatuor contineat conſtantes arbitrarias, vtique continet integrale completum noſtrae aequationis. Notum autem eſt bina poſteriora membra imaginaria reduci ad ſinum et coſinum anguli realis $\frac{s}{f}$. Hinc igitur multiplicando per communem factorem N, qui, ob tempus $t$ conſtans aſſumtum, pro functione temporis quacunque haberi poteſt, habebimus
$$y = N\left(\alpha e^{\frac{s}{f}} + \beta e^{\frac{-s}{f}} + \gamma \,\text{ſin.}\, \tfrac{s}{f} + \delta \,\text{coſ.}\, \tfrac{s}{f}\right);$$
qui ergo valor ante inuento $y = M \,\text{ſin.}\left(\zeta + t\sqrt{\tfrac{2g}{k}}\right)$ aequalis reddi debet, id quod facillime praeſtabitur ſtatuendo:
$$N = C \,\text{ſin.}\left(\zeta + t\sqrt{\tfrac{2g}{k}}\right) \text{ et}$$
$$M = C\left(\alpha e^{\frac{s}{f}} + \beta e^{\frac{-s}{f}} + \gamma \,\text{ſin.}\, \tfrac{s}{f} + \delta \,\text{coſ.}\, \tfrac{s}{f}\right),$$
ſic enim vterque valor reducetur ad iſtam aequationem:
$$y = C\left(\text{ſin.}\left(\zeta + t\sqrt{\tfrac{2g}{k}}\right)\right)\left(\alpha e^{\frac{s}{f}} + \beta e^{\frac{-s}{f}} + \gamma \,\text{ſin.}\, \tfrac{s}{f} + \delta \,\text{coſ.}\, \tfrac{s}{f}\right),$$
vbi iam literae $C, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, cum angulo $\zeta$ denotant veras quantitates conſtantes pro arbitrio accipiendas; quomodocunque autem accipiantur motus virgae ſemper ita erit comparatus, vt congruat cum oſcillationibus penduli
Acta Acad. Imp. Sc. Tom. III. P. I. \quad P \quad ſimpli-

items.english: This form, since it contains four arbitrary constants, certainly contains the complete integral of our equation.

items.quote: quomodocunque autem accipiantur motus virgae ſemper ita erit comparatus, vt congruat cum oſcillationibus penduli
items.english: However they are chosen, the motion of the rod will always be such that it agrees with the oscillations of a simple pendulum.
